chunks: Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Abu Ja'far, from al-'Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Hammad ibn 'Isa, from Hariz ibn 'Abd Allah, from Abu Basir, Zurarah, and Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام said: The people were ruined through their bellies and their private parts, because they did not render to us our right. Lo, indeed our Shi'ah, with regard to that, and their fathers, are in absolution.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Amir al-Mu'minin, the title of Imam 'Ali عليه السلام
key_terms.بُطُونِهِمْ: their bellies; meaning what they consume
key_terms.حَقَّنَا: our right; the due belonging to the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام
key_terms.شِيعَتَنَا: our Shi'ah; the followers of the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام
key_terms.فُرُوجِهِمْ: their private parts; meaning sexual relations
key_terms.فِي حِلٍّ: in absolution; released from liability in this matter

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith in al-Istibsar explain the Shi'ah being in absolution regarding khums in the time of ghaybah?
ai.summary: This hadith states that people fell into destruction through what they consumed and through sexual relations because they failed to deliver the right of the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام. It further declares that the Shi'ah are granted absolution regarding that matter, which in the chapter context relates to what was made permissible to them from khums during the ghaybah.
